They were led by second-year head coach [[Kevin Willard]] and played their home games at [[Xfinity Center (College Park, Maryland)|Xfinity Center]] in [[College Park, Maryland]], as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 16–17, 7–13 in [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for 12th place. As the No. 12 seed in the [[2024 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2023–24 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]] in the first round before losing to [[2023–24 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] 87-56. The team declined an offer to play in the postseason NIT. The Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team drew an average home attendance of 13,283 in 17 games in 2023-24.{{Cite web |title=MEN’S BASKETBALL ATTENDANCE RECORDS THROUGH 2024-25 |url=http://fs.ncaa.org.s3.amazonaws.com/Docs/stats/m_basketball_RB/Attend.pdf |access-date=3 Oct 2025 |website=NCAA}} ==Previous season== The [[2022–23 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Terrapins]] finished the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2022–23 season]] 22–13, 11–9 in [[2022–23 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fifth place. As the No. 6 seed in the [[2023 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2022–23 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] in the second round before losing to [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]] as the No. 8 seed in the South region.
